 Assignment Specific Feedback 


User-defined Functions:

Positive:
•  Good use of the following:
      - docstring - providing context; stating what the function does
      - docstring - clearly defining all input variables/objects
      - docstring - clearly defining the returned object(s)
      - internal check - proper use of 'if not isinstance', 'raise' statements, etc.
      - isolating ideas to user-defined functions
      - type hinting - applied well for input variables (and for what is returned, if applicable)

Negative:
•  Your user-defined functions had the following problems:
      - structure - main code logic should be nested under the internal checks (e.g., within an else statement) for clear flow control


Function (and Method) Calling:

Negative:
      - keyword arguments calls - include the parameter that are being assigned the argument to (e.g., 'my_function(param1=arg1, param2=arg2)'. Doing so ensure that the arguments are passed correctly.


Unit Test DNA Transcription:

Positive:
•  Additional user-defined function feedback:
      - Nice idea to provide default value for some of the parameters.
      - Good approach converting input to uppercase and then replacing `T` with `U`.
      - Good input validation: raising `TypeError` for non-string input.
      - Good input validation: raising `ValueError` for invalid nucleotides.
      - Very good job on incorporating the unit test concepts into your user-defined function development.
•  Exception testing done well:
      - For `unittest` - good use of `with self.assertRaises(ValueError)` to verify that invalid characters raise an error in the most concise manner.
•  Toy data generation:
      - Good use of random module (e.g., `random.randint`, `random.choices`) to create randomized toy data.
•  Overall unit test feedback:
      - Good job on using the unittest module/library.
      - You created a good transcription user-defined function.
      - Your unit tests correctly check your function.
      - Tests are readable and follow a logical naming scheme.

Neutral:
•  General feedback:
      - Toy data - consider including a validation for invalid ranges (e.g., negative sequence lengths).
      - Consider including testing edge cases (e.g., `TTTT`, `CtGg`, `GAGA`).
